clue.text: One inhabiting South America adopts custom in food

indicators.note: to adopt is to take on, so the South America letters take on the custom word after them

parts.note: one who lives in a place is a liver, a dweller
a custom is a usage, an established practice

explanation.surface: A resident of South America takes up a local custom in what they eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One inhabiting' reads as a description of a person, but it is a dweller, a LIVER. LIVER SAUSAGE is a soft spreading sausage made from liver.
explanation.definitionFit: A liver sausage is a cooked meat spread, so it is a kind of food.

clue.text: Saying little, cast coin into French lake

indicators.note: the reworked coin letters go into the French word for lake, so into marks the insertion

parts.note: lac is French for lake

indicators.note: to cast metal is to shape it anew, so the letters of coin are remoulded

explanation.surface: Someone tight-lipped tosses a coin into a lake in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' turns COIN into ONI, which goes into LAC to give LA-CONI-C.
explanation.definitionFit: Terse speech uses few words, which is what laconic describes.

clue.text: Going by tube you'd be unlikely to cross this?

definitions.text: Going by tube you'd be unlikely to cross this?

parts.words: Going by tube you'd be unlikely to cross this?
parts.note: an underground traveller never goes over a bridge carrying a railway across a valley; read cryptically, 'by' is the Latin-derived word for by way of and 'tube' is a pipe

explanation.surface: A London Underground passenger wonders what they never get to travel over.
explanation.walkthrough: The tube is London's Underground railway, which runs below ground and so rarely crosses a bridge. The clue also splits as 'by' (VIA) plus 'tube' (DUCT).
explanation.definitionFit: A long bridge of arches carrying a road or railway over a valley is something a train crosses.

clue.text: A decline in seating, it's said

indicators.note: it's said means the words are heard spoken rather than spelt out

parts.note: in means about, RE, and a seating is a sitting or session, giving RE plus SESSION

explanation.surface: Someone reports that fewer seats are being taken.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (about, from 'in') plus SESSION (a seating, a sitting of a body) sounds like RECESSION.
explanation.definitionFit: A recession is a period of economic downturn, a falling-off in trade.

clue.text: Church leader in one's very black books?

parts.note: one is A, the indefinite article
BB marks a very black, soft pencil lead
OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books

explanation.surface: A clergyman with a terrible record is in very bad odour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in one's very black books' suggests disgrace, but it breaks into A, BB (pencil grade) and OT (Old Testament).
explanation.definitionFit: An abbot heads a monastery, a senior figure in the church.

clue.text: Run south with holidaymaker?

indicators.note: with places the holidaymaker beside the south letter, following it

parts.note: a camper is someone on holiday in a tent or caravan

explanation.surface: A tourist heads off southwards at a trot.
explanation.definitionFit: To scamper is to run quickly and lightly.

clue.text: Departed, we hear, with odd load in boat

indicators.note: with joins the second piece after the first
we hear marks a word to be taken by its sound

parts.note: departed means gone, which is said like 'gon'

indicators.note: odd means strange, so the letters of load are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has left in a vessel carrying an awkward cargo.
explanation.walkthrough: GONE said aloud gives GON; 'odd' turns LOAD into DOLA.
explanation.definitionFit: A gondola is a flat-bottomed Venetian rowing vessel.

clue.text: Francs as coin would be inappropriate here

definitions.text: Francs as coin would be inappropriate here

indicators.note: inappropriate suggests things wrongly arranged, so the letters are put in another order

explanation.surface: French currency would be no use in a certain American city.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of FRANCS AS COIN rearrange to the city; and the whole clue is true, since a US city takes dollars, not francs.
explanation.definitionFit: A Californian city uses the dollar, so francs would be the wrong money there.

clue.text: Account includes repair of chair that's old

indicators.note: includes means the account letters hold the reworked chair inside
a repair rebuilds something, so the letters of chair are reassembled

explanation.surface: A bill covers mending an antique chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repair of' turns CHAIR into RCHAI, set inside AC.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic describes something belonging to an earlier time, antiquated.

clue.text: Magistrate has silly nit arrested, an unconventional type

indicators.note: arrested means held, so the magistrate letters hold the other piece

parts.note: beak is British slang for a magistrate

indicators.note: silly means foolish or jumbled, so the letters of nit are rearranged

explanation.surface: A judge has a foolish hippie taken into custody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' makes TNI from NIT, held inside BEAK. 'Beak' is British slang for a magistrate.
explanation.definitionFit: A beatnik was a 1950s bohemian who rejected conventional society.

clue.text: Barrister unemployed since 1952?

parts.note: a senior barrister's title follows the monarch; with a queen on the throne from 1952 the male-titled version would have had no holders

explanation.surface: A lawyer has been out of work for decades.
explanation.walkthrough: Elizabeth II came to the throne in 1952, so senior barristers became Queen's Counsel; the King's version had no work until 2022.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior barrister appointed under a king carries this title, so the title was unused during a queen's reign.

clue.text: Rag scores as means of raising money for charity?

definitions.text: means of raising money for charity?

parts.note: rag means teasing or fun, as in student rag week
runs are scores in cricket

explanation.surface: A student rag week tallies up its fundraising efforts.
explanation.walkthrough: Rag week is a British student charity festival, which supports the surface. In cricket, points are scored as runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Sponsored jogging events collect donations for good causes.

clue.text: Poor python gets nothing to eat in storm

indicators.note: to eat means the reworked snake swallows the other letter
poor means bad or broken, so the letters of python are rearranged

parts.note: O is the round figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A hungry snake is given no food during bad weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' turns PYTHON into TYPHON, which takes in O to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A typhoon is a tropical cyclone in the western Pacific.

clue.text: A Glaswegian races to England?

parts.note: a Glaswegian, from Glasgow, is a Scot

explanation.surface: A man from Glasgow heads south to England for a day at the racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot is an English racecourse, so a Scot going 'to England' for the races fits both the wordplay and the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal Ascot is a famous horse-racing meeting in Berkshire, England.

clue.text: They're cool solving crime case

indicators.note: solving a case means sorting it out, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Detectives keep calm while cracking a criminal case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cool' points to calm detectives, but here it means cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Frozen desserts are cold, so they are literally cool.

clue.text: An alternative to vermicide?

parts.note: a vermicide kills worms; the proverb says the first riser catches the worm, which would do the same job

explanation.surface: Someone asks what else might deal with worms.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'the early bird catches the worm' makes a bird an alternative to a worm-killing chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rises early is said to catch the worm, as the proverb puts it.

clue.text: It'll cope with one full of beans, making one prance around

definitions.text: It'll cope with one full of beans

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the letters of one prance are mixed up

explanation.surface: An energetic person is made to dance about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one full of beans' looks like a lively person, but it is a tin of beans.
explanation.definitionFit: A tin full of beans is opened with this kitchen tool.

clue.text: Were any drunk at this celebration?

definitions.text: Were any drunk at this celebration?

indicators.note: drunk means unsteady, so the letters of were any are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether guests were tipsy at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of WERE ANY rearrange to the answer, and the whole clue describes a party where drinking is customary.
explanation.definitionFit: A festive party at midnight on 31 December often involves heavy drinking.

clue.text: Condition for volume is nothing

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
taken as written
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A rule says the sound level must be zero.
explanation.definitionFit: A proviso is a stipulation attached to an agreement.

clue.text: Copper seen on Spanish river: that's an interesting thing

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
rio is Spanish for river

explanation.surface: A police officer is spotted beside a river in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a police officer, but it is the metal, symbol CU.
explanation.definitionFit: A curio is a rare or unusual object, a curiosity.

clue.text: Company's board controlled Spanish city

indicators.note: controlled means managed or put in order, so the letters of board are arranged anew

explanation.surface: A firm's directors run a city in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'controlled' turns BOARD into RDOBA after CO.
explanation.definitionFit: Córdoba is a city in Andalusia, southern Spain.

clue.text: Stays on electricity supply

parts.note: re means on the subject of, on
the mains is the domestic supply of electricity

explanation.surface: Someone keeps the power switched on.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain is to stay put, so the verb forms match.

clue.text: Observed navy, badly reduced in size

parts.note: saw means observed
off means bad, as in food that has gone off

explanation.surface: Someone noticed the fleet had been cut back severely.
explanation.walkthrough: SAWN-OFF describes something like a shotgun with its barrel cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: A sawn-off item has had part cut away, making it shorter.

clue.text: Ascetic's just about king

indicators.note: about means around, so the just letters go around the king letter

parts.note: just means fair
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A holy man is described as fair-minded towards the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A fakir is a Muslim or Hindu holy man living in self-denial.

clue.text: Worker found squirrel's nest over on island

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the letters of the squirrel's nest word are read backwards

parts.note: a drey or dray is a squirrel's nest
Man is the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A labourer comes across a squirrel's nest on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns DRAY into YARD; MAN is the Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardman is a labourer who works in a railway or timber yard.

clue.text: Bloke is ordered to make a pillar

indicators.note: ordered means put in a new sequence, so the letters of bloke is are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man is commanded to build a column.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like a command, but here it means arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An obelisk is a tall tapering stone column.

clue.text: Put on a pedestal that is solid in construction

indicators.note: in places the reworked solid letters inside the that-is letters

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation for 'that is', id est

indicators.note: a construction is something built, so the letters of solid are put together anew

explanation.surface: Placing a statue on a plinth is sturdy building work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'construction' turns SOLID into DOLIS, which sits in IE.
explanation.definitionFit: To worship someone excessively is to treat them as an idol raised above others.

clue.text: Vehicles right in love and sacred in conflict

indicators.note: in puts the right letter inside the love word

parts.note: amour is a love affair, love

indicators.note: in conflict means at odds, so the letters of sacred are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Romance and holiness are at war over some vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right in love' puts R inside AMOUR to give ARMOUR; 'in conflict' turns SACRED into EDCARS.
explanation.definitionFit: Armoured cars are military vehicles protected by steel plating.
